subtitle: How a Feudatory from Malwa Struck the Lion in Its Den

panels.shot: epic wide shot from behind Siyaka on a rocky ridge, overlooking a distant fortified city in the Deccan haze
panels.action: Siyaka II stands silhouetted on a crag above a broad plain, his cloak stirred by dry wind, as far away the low sprawl of an Indian capital city glimmers under the harsh sun.

dialogue.text: In 972, a lesser lord from Malwa chased the Rashtrakuta king to Manyakheta—and struck the empire’s own capital. How did a feudatory dare to unmake his masters?

i18n.hi: ९७२ में मालवा का एक छोटा सरदार राष्ट्रकूट राजा को दौड़ाते‑दौड़ाते मैयखेता तक ले गया—और साम्राज्य की अपनी राजधानी पर चोट कर बैठा। एक सामंत ने हिम्मत कैसे की?

panels.shot: slow push-in over a map-like aerial of central India, rivers and regions softly lit as if inked on old palm-leaf charts
panels.action: A bird’s-eye vision of the subcontinent shows the Narmada curving between plateau and Deccan, with the lands of Malwa to the north and the Deccan plateau stretching south.

dialogue.text: In the mid-tenth century, Malwa lay on a frontier of power. North of the Narmada, new houses stirred. South of it, the Rashtrakuta emperors ruled from Manyakheta.

i18n.hi: दसवीं सदी के बीच, मालवा ताक़त की सरहद पर था। नर्मदा के उत्तर नए घराने उठ रहे थे। दक्षिण में मैयखेता से राष्ट्रकूट सम्राट राज चला रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of Siyaka in a court pavilion, low angle to show his youth yet subordinate status
panels.action: Young Siyaka II sits on a simple throne under a wooden pavilion, his face alert but restrained, while in the background a Rashtrakuta emblem hangs as a reminder of suzerainty.

dialogue.text: The Harsola copper plates of 949 name Siyaka of the Paramaras, granting land under Rashtrakuta shadow. He is no sovereign yet, but a feudatory threading loyalty and ambition.

i18n.hi: ९४९ की हर्सोला ताम्रपट्ट में परमार सियाका का नाम है, राष्ट्रकूट साए में मिली ज़मीन के साथ। अभी वह राजा नहीं, पर वफ़ादारी और महत्वाकांक्षा दोनों बुनता सामंत है।

panels.shot: close-up on Siyaka’s hands holding a copper plate charter, candlelight catching the engraved letters
panels.action: Siyaka gently holds an engraved copper plate, its writing gleaming as he studies it, the faint firelight emphasizing the script’s grooves and his intent expression.

dialogue.text: On those plates, his titles echo Rashtrakuta favour. Yet even there, the Paramara name stands firm—already a house on the Narmada frontier, watching the empire’s fortunes.

i18n.hi: उन्हीं पट्टों में उसके ख़िताब राष्ट्रकूट मेहरबानी गूँजाते हैं। पर ‘परमार’ नाम अडिग है—नर्मदा की सरहद पर बैठा, साम्राज्य की किस्मत नापता घराना।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Narmada valley, troops moving like small lines across the riverine landscape
panels.action: Columns of armoured horsemen and foot soldiers wind along the stony banks of the Narmada, with scrub forests and rocky outcrops framing their cautious advance.

dialogue.text: By the 970s, that frontier is a battlefield. Later inscriptions recall Siyaka’s clash with Khottiga, Rashtrakuta king, near the Narmada—the north testing the old Deccan lion.

i18n.hi: ९७० के दशक तक वही सरहद रणभूमि बन चुकी थी। बाद के लेख सियाका की नर्मदा के पास राष्ट्रकूट राजा खोट्टिग के संग भिड़ंत याद रखते हैं—उत्तर, बूढ़े दक्खिनी शेर को परखता है।

panels.shot: dynamic mid-wide from ground level, Siyaka on horseback facing south as dust clouds rise
panels.action: Siyaka sits firm on his horse at the river’s edge, gaze turned south, while faint dust plumes on the horizon suggest a distant, retreating force.

dialogue.speaker: siyaka_ii
dialogue.text: They run for Manyakheta. If we stop here, we remain vassals forever.

i18n.hi: वे मैयखेता भाग रहे हैं। अगर यहीं रुके, तो हमेशा के लिए जागीरदार ही रहेंगे।

panels.shot: three-quarter rear shot following Siyaka’s horsemen as they ford the Narmada, water splashing around them
panels.action: Siyaka urges his horse through the shallows of the Narmada, his retinue close behind, as the river’s current breaks around hooves in glittering spray.

dialogue.text: The records do not linger on tactics. They remember the decision: Siyaka crossed the Narmada in pursuit. Feudatory banners now ride into the Deccan heartland.

i18n.hi: बही‑खातों में चालों का वर्णन नहीं, बस फ़ैसला दर्ज है: सियाका नर्मदा पार कर के पीछा करता गया। सामंती ध्वज अब दक्खिन के दिल में घुस चले।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot of a long march, silhouettes against changing landscapes from Malwa plateau to Deccan plains
panels.action: A stretched column of riders and footmen appears in silhouette, moving from stony plateau to open plain, with changing trees and soil hinting at their journey southward.

dialogue.text: Day by day, Malwa’s men follow the retreating Rashtrakutas. Across plateaus and dry forests, the road leads to a name whispered with awe—Manyakheta, seat of emperors.

i18n.hi: दिन‑दिन भर, मालवा के सिपाही पीछे हटते राष्ट्रकूटों के पीछे चलते रहे। पठारों और सूखे जंगलों को पार करती राह एक नाम पर जा थमती है—मैयखेता, सम्राटों का आसन।

panels.shot: establishing wide shot of Manyakheta from a distance, its walls low but sprawling, smoke of hearths rising in the evening
panels.action: The city of Manyakheta spreads across the plain, with earth-and-brick fortifications, clustered roofs, and thin streams of smoke rising into the dusk sky.

dialogue.text: Manyakheta, in today’s Karnataka, had long anchored Rashtrakuta might. Here, kings issued grants and poets praised them. Now, an enemy from Malwa appears at its edge.

i18n.hi: आज के कर्नाटक की मैयखेता सदियों से राष्ट्रकूट ताक़त की जड़ थी। यहीं से फ़रमान निकलते, कवि राजाओं का गान करते। अब मालवा का दुश्मन इसकी देहलीज़ पर आ खड़ा है।

panels.shot: medium-wide shot just outside the city walls, defenders in anxious readiness as dust clouds approach
panels.action: Guardians stand tense atop a city wall, looking out at rising dust and faint glints of armed men advancing across the plain.

dialogue.text: Our sources are sparse on the fight itself. Later prashastis speak of a capital humbled; Dhanapala, writing close in time, speaks of a lord of Malava looting Manyakheta.

i18n.hi: लड़ाई का ब्योरा हमारे पास कम है। बाद की प्रशस्तियाँ राजधानी के झुके सिर की बात करती हैं; लगभग समकालीन धनपाल लिखता है—मालवाधिपति ने मैयखेता लूटी।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Siyaka before the city, raising his arm to signal, his face taut
panels.action: Siyaka stands at the head of his men before the city’s outer area, his arm lifted in a measured signal, his expression controlled and grim.

dialogue.speaker: siyaka_ii
dialogue.text: Remember this: beyond these walls lies not just plunder, but our place in history.

i18n.hi: याद रखो: इन दीवारों के पार सिर्फ़ माल नहीं, हमारी इतिहास में जगह पड़ी है।

panels.shot: tight medium of Siyaka moving through a breached quarter, focus on his face against a backdrop of chaos
panels.action: Siyaka advances through a city street in turmoil, buildings scorched, people fleeing in the distance, his eyes scanning with hard, unreadable calm.

dialogue.text: We are not told of numbers, of slaughter or mercy in detail. We are told that the Rashtrakuta capital was sacked—that its wealth and pride fell into Paramara hands.

i18n.hi: न हमें फ़ौजों की गिनती मिलती है, न कत्लेआम या दया की कथा। बस इतना लिखा है कि राष्ट्रकूट राजधानी लूटी गई—दौलत और शान, दोनों परमार हाथों में गईं।

panels.shot: medium shot of Siyaka in an inner courtyard, his men carrying chests and goods past him while he stands still
panels.action: In a modest inner court, Siyaka stands as his soldiers carry heavy chests and bundled goods away, the scene one of controlled plunder rather than frenzy.

dialogue.text: Dhanapala’s preface notes simply that the lord of Malava was looting Manyakheta. A contemporary witness reduces an imperial city to a scene of spoils.

i18n.hi: धनपाल की भूमिका बस इतना नोट करती है कि मालवाधिपति मैयखेता लूट रहा था। एक समकालीन नज़र में साम्राज्य‑नगर महज़ ग़नीमत का मैदान रह गया।

panels.shot: wide shot of the city skyline darkened by smoke columns, with birds wheeling above
panels.action: Smoke columns rise from parts of Manyakheta, darkening the sky as birds wheel uneasily over the dim outline of shrines and halls.

dialogue.text: The details of ruin are lost. Yet this much is clear in the record: the Rashtrakuta capital suffered a sack at the hands of a frontier chief from Malwa.

i18n.hi: विनाश की सूक्ष्म कहानी खो गई। पर इतना साफ़ दर्ज है: राष्ट्रकूट राजधानी को मालवा की सरहदी सरदार ने लूट की मार झेलाई।

panels.shot: medium-close of Siyaka on the return march, framed against a laden caravan and weary soldiers
panels.action: Siyaka rides at the head of a returning column, pack animals and weary troops trailing behind, the load of captured goods evident in the slow, heavy movement.

dialogue.text: With spoils and prestige, Siyaka turned north again. Behind him, Manyakheta’s aura of invincibility was cracked; ahead, Malwa’s status in the political chessboard had changed.

i18n.hi: माल‑मत्ता और मान लेकर सियाका फिर उत्तर की ओर मुड़ा। पीछे मैयखेता की अजेयता टूट चुकी थी; आगे राजनीति की बिसात पर मालवा की चाल बदल चुकी थी।

panels.shot: low-angle medium of Siyaka seated once more in his Malwa court, now with different regalia around him
panels.action: Back in Malwa, Siyaka sits on his seat again, but this time surrounded by richer ornaments and more confident nobles, his bearing subtly more assured.

dialogue.text: Later prashastis of the Paramaras look back to this exploit as a turning. From a feudatory grant in 949 to the sack of 972–973, Siyaka’s arc marks the birth of a sovereign house.

i18n.hi: परमारों की बाद की प्रशस्तियाँ इस कारनामे को मोड़ मानती हैं। ९४९ की जागीर से ९७२–९७३ की लूट तक, सियाका की रेखा एक स्वतंत्र वंश के जन्म को दिखाती है।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot of a Rashtrakuta emblem fading while a Paramara emblem sharpens into focus
panels.action: In a stylized composition, a carved Rashtrakuta emblem appears eroded and dim, while beside it a sharp, newly carved Paramara symbol stands out against polished stone.

dialogue.text: For the Rashtrakutas, the blow at Manyakheta signalled decline. For Malwa, it opened a path that would lead, in time, to Bhoja and the famed Paramara kingdom.

i18n.hi: राष्ट्रकूटों के लिए मैयखेता की चोट ढलान का इशारा थी। मालवा के लिए यही रास्ता आगे चलकर भोज और प्रसिद्ध परमार साम्राज्य तक पहुँचा।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Siyaka’s weathered face in late middle age, eyes distant as if seeing both river and capital
panels.action: An older Siyaka sits quietly, his face lined, eyes distant, as if weighing the memory of a river crossed and a capital taken.

dialogue.text: We do not hear Siyaka’s own words, only the echoes of scribes and poets. Yet in their lines, one act stands clear: a feudatory striking his suzerain’s capital, and not turning back.

i18n.hi: हम स्वयं सियाका की ज़ुबान नहीं सुनते, सिर्फ़ लेखकों‑कवियों की गूँज सुनते हैं। पर उनकी पंक्तियों में एक काम साफ़ है: सामंत ने अपने अधिपति की राजधानी पर वार किया—और पीछे नहीं मुड़ा।

panels.shot: final wide shot of the Narmada at sunset, Siyaka’s faint figure on the bank, the sky reflecting in the river
panels.action: The Narmada glows under a setting sun, its surface bronze and calm, with a small, almost ghostly figure of Siyaka standing on its bank, gazing south.

dialogue.text: Siyaka at Manyakheta reminds us that a frontier lord’s decision—to cross a river, to pursue an emperor—can redraw realms, and that the map of India was often changed by such bold breaks.

i18n.hi: मैयखेता में सियाका याद दिलाता है कि सरहदी सरदार का फ़ैसला—नदी पार करना, सम्राट का पीछा करना—पूरे मुल्क बदल सकता है, और भारत का नक्शा अक्सर ऐसी दिलेर टक्कर से ही नया बना।

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Feudatory from Malwa Struck the Lion in Its Den
subtitle_i18n.hi: मालवा के सामंत ने शेर को उसके अड्डे पर कैसे गरदा चटाया
